security_spec.violation_condition: In XiangShan's NewCSR implementation (SupervisorLevel.scala:30), sie reads from mie when mideleg(bit)=1 via combinatorial alias (val mieIsAlias = mideleg), but mie's write logic (MachineLevel.scala:55-120) only explicitly forwards SSIE(bit1), STIE(bit5), SEIE(bit9), and local IE bits from sie. If LCOFIE(bit13) is categorized outside both the explicit non-local forwarding and the getLocal iteration—or if any interrupt enable bit handled by getLocal behaves inconsistently with the explicit handlers—then a write to sie.LCOFIE when mideleg.LCOFI=1 is silently dropped: sie.toMie fires valid→true for the bit, but mie's fromSie handler for that bit is a no-op. S-mode software believes it enabled LCOFI interrupts via sie, but mie.LCOFIE remains unchanged, and the interrupt never fires. Additionally, mideleg transitions are purely combinational (no synchronization pipeline stage), so a CSR write to mideleg that changes delegation status can race with a concurrent or closely-spaced write to sie on the same cycle or the next, causing the sie write to land on the wrong target (mie vs. internal reg) or be lost entirely.
security_spec.summary: sie→mie interrupt-enable alias forwarding chain may have incomplete bit coverage (LCOFIE at bit 13) and combinational mideleg-dependent alias switching creates a race window where sie writes can be silently dropped or misrouted between mie and the mvien internal register
